from todo import add_todo, complete_todo


def test_add_todo_appends_item():
    todos = []
    add_todo(todos, "buy milk")
    assert todos == [{"text": "buy milk", "done": False}]


def test_add_todo_empty_raises():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="item cannot be empty"):
        add_todo([], "")


def test_complete_todo_marks_done():

    complete_todo(todos, "buy milk")

display.text:
import pytest

from todo import add_todo, complete_todo


def test_add_todo_appends_item():
    todos = []
    add_todo(todos, "buy milk")
    assert todos == [{"text": "buy milk", "done": False}]


def test_add_todo_empty_raises():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="item cannot be empty"):
        add_todo([], "")


def test_complete_todo_marks_done():
    todos = [{"text": "buy milk", "done": False}]
    complete_todo(todos, "buy milk")
    assert todos == [{"text": "buy milk", "done": True}]


def test_complete_todo_not_found_raises():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="todo not found: buy milk"):
        complete_todo([], "buy milk")


def test_complete_todo_matches_first_duplicate_only():
    todos = [
        {"text": "buy milk", "done": False},
        {"text": "buy milk", "done": False},
    ]
    complete_todo(todos, "buy milk")
    assert todos == [
        {"text": "buy milk", "done": True},
        {"text": "buy milk", "done": False},
    ]


def test_add_then_complete_todo():
    todos = []
    add_todo(todos, "buy milk")
    complete_todo(todos, "buy milk")
    assert todos == [{"text": "buy milk", "done": True}]

part.text:
Before I touch `add_todo`/`complete_todo`, worth naming the design tension: those are currently pure functions, they take a list, mutate it, return it, no I/O. "Persist todos" means giving them a way to save to disk, but I don't want to force every call to hit the filesystem, since that would also break all 6 existing tests, which call these functions with just `(todos, item)`.

I'll thread it through with an optional `path=None` parameter: when omitted, behavior is identical to now (pure, in-memory, tests untouched); when given, the function saves via `storage.save_todos` after mutating. That's the minimal, backward-compatible way to add persistence without turning these into I/O-only functions.

from todo import add_todo, complete_todo
from storage import load_todos
import tempfile, os

path = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), 'todos_persist_test.json')
if os.path.exists(path):
    os.remove(path)

todos = []
add_todo(todos, 'buy milk', path=path)
add_todo(todos, 'walk dog', path=path)
complete_todo(todos, 'buy milk', path=path)

loaded = load_todos(path)
print(loaded)
assert loaded == todos
os.remove(path)
print('persistence ok')
"
